assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling turned aryl amination from a harsh, substrate-limited problem into a routine, general bond construction. It is the clearest example of a method that changed how chemists everywhere build bonds, with ligand design that gave conceptual simplicity.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig developed the general catalytic amination and the ligand classes that made it broadly usable; Kosugi's earlier tin-amide coupling was a precursor with limited scope. Two laureates is a natural, fair configuration, though the precursor credit would need acknowledgement.
assessment.maturity: Over 25 years of use in medicinal and process chemistry and countless total syntheses. Fully mature and independently confirmed; recognition is arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the committee wants to treat Kosugi's precursor work as disqualifying or merely historical.
Overlap with the cross-coupling Nobel (2010) may be argued as a mere extension; I judge the scope and ligand innovation chemically new.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis opened radical and open-shell pathways under mild conditions, enabling bond constructions that were not practical before, now widely used in discovery and process chemistry.
assessment.attribution: MacMillan, Yoon and Stephenson independently launched the field in 2008. Konig, Nicewicz, Melchiorre and Fukuzumi are also strong, so three-person limit creates a hard allocation. MacMillan already has a 2021 prize, which may weigh against him.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted with strong independent validation and industrial use, though the field is still evolving; timely rather than premature.
uncertainties: Credit allocation among seven names and MacMillan's prior prize.
Ru/Ir polypyridyl photochemistry has older roots, so the novelty of the synthetic application must be weighed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Selective C-H functionalization offers step-economy and a new logic of retrosynthesis, directly in line with efficiency in synthesis. Directing-group and ligand-controlled strategies from Yu and Sanford, and Ir-catalyzed borylation from Hartwig and Smith, are now applied in late-stage functionalization.
assessment.attribution: Yu (ligand-accelerated, directed and remote C-H activation), Sanford (Pd(II/IV) catalysis) and Hartwig (borylation) are the most decisive among the supplied names. Daugulis and Smith have real claims, so allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly growing adoption, but industrial routine use is still narrower than cross-coupling. Reasonably mature, slightly early.
uncertainties: Whether this is one discovery or several distinct methods needing different recognition.
Breadth of practical use compared with older coupling chemistry.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native chemical ligation made total chemical synthesis of proteins practical by joining unprotected peptide segments chemoselectively. This is genuinely new chemistry with broad impact on protein science.
assessment.attribution: Kent and Dawson reported native chemical ligation in 1994, and Muir developed expressed protein ligation and semisynthesis. Danishefsky contributed related ligation work, and Brik and Liu are later extensions. A Kent, Dawson, Muir trio is defensible.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of confirmation and use in synthetic proteins and chemical biology; mature and timely.
uncertainties: Relative weight of Kent versus Dawson on the original concept.
The border with chemical biology: I would ask what was chemically new, and here the chemoselective thioester exchange and S-to-N shift answer that.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Frustrated Lewis pairs showed that sterically hindered Lewis acid-base pairs activate H2 and other small molecules without metals, a new reactivity concept that gave metal-free hydrogenation.
assessment.attribution: Stephan discovered the metal-free H2 activation in 2006 and Erker contributed key developments of the concept; the two-person configuration is clean. Earlier related observations by others are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Fifteen to twenty years of independent confirmation. Conceptually fresh, but practical use in synthesis and industry is still limited, so it may be somewhat premature.
uncertainties: Practical impact beyond academic interest remains modest.
Earlier precedents of Lewis pair reactivity could complicate priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Intermolecular oxidative addition of unreactive alkane C-H bonds to iridium complexes proved that saturated hydrocarbons can be activated homogeneously, founding the field of C-H activation that underlies much of modern methodology.
assessment.attribution: Bergman's 1982 report is the decisive discovery. William Graham's contemporaneous work is not among the supplied names, and the credit list supports only Bergman, which leaves an attribution question.
assessment.maturity: Long confirmed and foundational; recognition is not premature. Practical catalytic alkane functionalization remains limited, which makes it more a concept than a general method.
uncertainties: Contemporaneous independent work by others not on the supplied list.
Impact is conceptual more than practical in routine synthesis.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Phosphoramidite chemistry made reliable automated oligonucleotide synthesis possible and underpins sequencing, PCR primers, gene synthesis and nucleic-acid drugs. It is a transformative synthetic method with enormous use.
assessment.attribution: Caruthers developed the phosphoramidite method and its solid-phase automation. Hood contributed to automated DNA synthesizer instrumentation rather than the core chemistry, so I credit Caruthers alone while noting that attribution is debatable.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of ubiquitous use; fully mature. Timeliness is long past, but the discovery is clear and important.
uncertainties: Whether the instrument-development credit to Hood justifies a second laureate.
Beaucage and other contributors to the underlying chemistry are not in the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom transfer radical polymerization provided controlled radical polymerization with predictable molecular weights and architectures using simple catalysts, with wide use in materials. It is a conceptually simple method that made hard control routine.
assessment.attribution: Matyjaszewski and Sawamoto reported the Cu and Ru-based systems in 1995 independently. Wang and Kamigaito are co-authors on those reports, so the choice of two laureates leaves a contested allocation.
assessment.maturity: Mature with extensive use, though competing methods such as RAFT and nitroxide-mediated polymerization share the field.
uncertainties: Overlap with RAFT and other controlled radical polymerizations affects how the field would be recognized.
Whether co-authors deserve credit alongside the two principals.
